verdict.rationale: The IRS publishes some delegation rules. A third-party designee may apply for an EIN with signed authorization from the responsible party (irs-supp-13). It defines a credentialed Authorized e-file Provider role with an enrollment and suitability path (irs-supp-5, irs-supp-6). It also states that signed mobile-friendly forms, including the 83(b) Form 15620, require the taxpayer's own Online Account behind ID.me biometric proofing, which marks those signatures as personal (irs-supp-12, irs-supp-9). This is scattered across individual services rather than one published map of what third parties may and may not do. Missing for 10: general power-of-attorney and authorization forms (e.g. representative or tax-information authorizations), a consolidated catalog of third-party roles and their scopes, explicit designee form details, and independent corroboration.
